_comment: Single machine-readable home for finance-pipeline constants (spec T6/T30/T32/T36). Prose/design rationale lives in vault/knowledge/design-finance-blockframe.md — never duplicate it here.

hi._chars_per_second_note: 14.281 measured 2026-08-08 across all 81 per-line clips of passive-income-number-hi on AMRUT (5,919 chars / 414.454s of audio). Was 13.03, measured on HARSH across first-lakh-first-thousand-hi and carried over on the assumption the voices matched. They do not: Amrut is 9.60% faster per line, and the drift was ONE-SIDED — 71 of 81 lines short against expected — which is the documented signature of a wrong key, not noise (see cuts.en._chars_per_second_trap; en showed 78/78). Ordering rule was already satisfied: the speech-time budget formula was corrected 2026-08-07, so raising the rate now does not un-cancel a second error. This is the FLAT delivered rate including pause silence, which is what script budgeting needs; pipeline_check adds tts.pause_seconds on top per line.
hi._voice_note: Creator pick 2026-08-07 after an A/B listening test: Amrut Deshmukh (Educational Hindi Voice) replaces Harsh (Clear & Calm Documentary Narrator), the locked channel voice since 2026-07-28. Chosen to match style E. Samples: studio/voice-tests/passive-income-number/. RUNTIME: free. ⚠ CORRECTED 2026-08-08 — this note previously said the two voices landed within 0.2s on a 58-second passage so no re-budget was needed. That was measured on a CONTINUOUS read, and it was wrong by 9.6% at the per-line level. A continuous read carries inter-sentence pause INSIDE the audio; per-line clips push that same pause out into lead_in + tail padding, where it stops counting as speech. Measure every future voice A/B on PER-LINE CLIPS or it will always under-report the flat rate by roughly the padding it absorbs. Same copy: 118.0s continuous vs 107.20s as 21 per-line clips.

en._chars_per_second_note: 17.57 = the mean of three FLAT measurements on the cuts we actually ship (first-lakh-first-thousand-en MEDIUM 17.73 · japanese-money-methods-en LONG 17.39 · passive-income-number-en MEDIUM 17.588). Raised from 16.1 on 2026-08-07, once the both-or-neither precondition below was finally met. ⚠ SHORT CAVEAT: the 16.1 it replaces was itself measured, on SHORT cuts (16.11, 16.64). The gap is mechanical, not noise — SHORT writes shorter lines, so punctuation-pause time is a bigger share of each clip and the flat chars/second comes out lower. This single key is now tuned for MEDIUM/LONG, which is all the channel has shipped since 2026-07-30. If a SHORT cut is ever made again, expect scripts ~9% long and re-measure before trusting this number.
en._chars_per_second_trap: RESOLVED 2026-08-07 — kept as the record of how it was resolved, because the ordering rule still applies to the hi key. The bug was never the rate alone: fin-script budgeted chars as target_seconds × rate, which ignores the per-line scene padding that is not audio, so a wrong rate and a wrong formula cancelled and both cuts still hit target. Fixing either one alone breaks that cancellation — raising the rate first would have made every script ~17% long. Order followed: (1) fin-script and fin-audit both derived (target − lines × (lead_in + tail)) × rate independently on passive-income-number and logged the override; (2) the orchestrator's confirm-block formula was corrected in .claude/commands/finance-video.md; (3) only then was chars_per_second raised. Evidence that the key was wrong rather than noisy: across 78 lines of passive-income-number-en, ALL 78 drifted negative against expected_seconds. Noise is two-sided; a wrong key is one-sided.

tts._pause_seconds_note: Silence the voice actually takes at each mark, added to the flat chars/rate estimate in pipeline_check.expected_seconds. Without it the cold-open hook — short punched clauses, the winning format in this niche — self-flags as truncated: first-lakh-first-thousand line 1.1 measured 5.88s against a 3.84s flat estimate (+53%) purely from one danda and one em-dash. Symmetric tolerance means this makes genuinely SHORT clips easier to catch, not harder.

short._disk_note: 3.0 measured, not estimated: the good-debt/credit-history pairs came in at 2.81 GB stills-only (fin, 2026-07-30). Was 1.0. Add ~3 GB more per pair if the run uses footage — see video_scene.disk_gb_per_cut_extraction. doctor reserves 2x this.

medium._disk_note: 6.0 extrapolated from the measured SHORT figure at ~2.9x the runtime (fin, 2026-07-30). Was 3.0.

scene._transition_note: Cross-dissolve length. EVERY scene but the last carries data-duration = its duration + this, so the outgoing scene is still on screen while the incoming one fades in. Root duration is unaffected. See tools/scaffold/assets/js/motion.js.
scene._scene_seconds_note: One VO line = one clip = one scene, so scene COUNT is emergent from the script, never a constant. These bound the felt pace instead: aim ~6.5s per scene, and check_build FAILS any scene holding one photo past max_scene_seconds. Creator 2026-07-31: '9 scenes are too low for medium size video ... looks professional and engaging not dead.' The `lines: 9` on the SHORT tier and on the architecture entries is a SHORT-tier constant — fin-script.md is explicit that at MEDIUM/LONG 'none of the 9-segment constants apply'.
scene._lead_tail_tier_note: lead_in/tail are charged PER LINE, so they scale with line count and a value tuned at SHORT's 9 lines is wrong at MEDIUM's ~86. At 0.4+1.0 the hi cut spent 120.4s of its 566s on inter-line padding; with tts.pause_seconds already buying 80.5s of in-line pause that is 35% of the video in silence. MEDIUM/LONG override to 0.25+0.55 (68.8s), landing 514.8s against the 510s target. Creator 2026-07-31: 'looks professional and engaging not dead.'

_architectures_note: The pipeline ROTATES these — `pipeline_check.py architecture` returns the one least recently used, and the orchestrator writes it into run.json before fin-script runs. Six consecutive blockframe-9 cuts shipped because the only control was a warning written into notes that no code read; the fix is that the default now varies by construction rather than being flagged after the fact. Add an entry here to put a new layout into the rotation.
_architecture_lock_note: When set, this WINS over the rotation above and every run uses it — no per-run override, nothing to remember. Creator decision 2026-07-30: the creator reviewed all thirteen candidate styles side by side (nine of them registry-backed) and chose to keep blockframe-9, so the rotation would otherwise hand the next run ledger-rail and silently contradict a decision that was actually made. A lock is the honest representation of 'we picked one'. Delete this key to resume rotating; `doctor` refuses a lock that names an architecture that does not exist, so a typo cannot degrade to silent rotation. The sameness risk this rotation existed to manage is now carried by the non-layout levers instead — transitions (live), the SFX kit (present), and the music bed (see tools/audio/kit.json).
_image_per_scene_note: HARD creator rule, restated 2026-07-30 while rejecting most of the thirteen candidate styles: 'images are compulsury'. Every architecture MUST declare image_per_scene: true and actually carry a photograph in EVERY frame — a style that renders type on flat colour is out of scope no matter how good it looks. `doctor` refuses an architecture without the flag, so a new style cannot be added that quietly drops the image. Pairs with layout.photo_free_scene_ratio = 0.
_styles_rejected_note: Reviewed and rejected 2026-07-30 — do not re-propose without new reason. 'news-ticker': we are not making news videos, irrelevant to finance education. 'code-snippet' and 'code-typing': we are not making coding videos. The other registry directions were rejected for carrying no photograph; the ones that can be re-cut to carry one may return. 'x-post'/'reddit-post' was ACCEPTED as an occasional component (not an architecture) — usable only when a real, topical social post exists; see _components.

social-quote.use: Quote a REAL, topical social post (X or Reddit) inside a scene when one genuinely relates to the video's argument. A component, never a whole architecture, and never fabricated — an invented post is a fabricated fact and breaks the never-invent rule.
social-quote.caution: Real posts mean real usernames and real people on screen. Prefer posts from institutional or public accounts; do not put a private individual's handle in a monetised video criticising their money decisions.

_stock_video_note: SUPPORTED — corrected 2026-07-30 (an earlier version of this note said the opposite; it was wrong). HyperFrames does not play video in real time: it pre-extracts the clip to frames with ffmpeg and injects the right one as an before each capture (studio/packages/engine/src/services/videoFrameInjector.ts), so rendering stays deterministic. We have already shipped it — compositions/video-02-claude-edits-video/index.html has eight root

video_scene._note: Load-bearing rules for footage behind a scene. The first one is the trap: it renders BLACK and no linter catches it.
video_scene.must_be_root_child: A <video> MUST be a direct child of #root. Our .bg is a div inside <section class='scene'> — a <video> placed there renders black. Hoist footage to root siblings and give that scene's .scene background: transparent, or its opaque --bg paints over the footage.
video_scene.no_ken_on_video: Never apply `ken` to footage — real camera motion and a Ken Burns push fight each other.
video_scene._duration_note: A clip shorter than its scene freezes on its last frame. Scenes run 11-28s and stock clips 8-20s, so pre-loop at fetch time with ffmpeg rather than discovering it at render.

vector_art._note: Icons and flat-illustration Lotties. Both sit ON the graded photograph, never instead of it (image_per_scene is a hard rule). Rationale, licence and the two silent-blank traps: vault/knowledge/design-icons-emoji-lottie.md. Components: .icon / .lottie / .aside in blockframe.css. Motion: draw / loadLottie / playLottie in motion.js.
vector_art.library: assets/ — git-tracked, OUTSIDE studio/ (which is gitignored and deleted per cut). REUSE BEFORE YOU FETCH: search the library first, and save back anything you had to fetch or draw, so the next video finds it locally. assets/lottie/<name>.json (pristine, untinted) + <name>.png (preview) + index.json (tags/source/licence/used_in); assets/icons/<name>.svg. See assets/README.md.
vector_art.icon_first: An icon, arrow, chart mark or currency glyph is an inline <svg class='icon'> animated with draw() — no player, no asset, and the stroke takes a palette colour via currentColor. Reach for Lottie only when the graphic is a real illustration that would take an hour to rebuild.
vector_art.emoji: Not the icon system. A colour emoji renders correctly but is an OS font (tofu on a machine without one) and sits outside the grade, so it reads as a sticker on a film. Deliberate tonal break only.

lottie.search: tools/lottie/search.py "<phrase>" --sheet — prints the LIBRARY matches first (with their own contact sheet) and only then the remote candidates. Fetching something the library already holds is the failure mode this exists to prevent.
lottie.save_back: tools/lottie/search.py --save "<cell>=<name>" --tags "a,b,c" — writes the pristine asset into assets/lottie/. Do this BEFORE tinting: the library never stores a pre-coloured file, and an asset that skips this step is one the next video has to find again.
lottie.license: Lottie Simple License (free catalogue only): commercial use ok, modification ok, NO attribution required, must not redistribute the raw file. The premium marketplace needs a paid plan and is not used.
lottie.vector_only: Reject any asset whose assets[] carry a "p" (embedded bitmap) — it cannot be re-tinted and it will not scale to 1080p.
lottie.tint: tools/lottie/tint.py <library-name> studio/videos/<slug>-<cut>/assets/lottie/<n>.js <accent-hex> — REQUIRED. Stock art arrives in someone else's colours and lands on the grade as clip-art; the tint maps it onto a panel->accent->ink ramp by luminance. Accent = the scene's role colour (fund/target/warn).
lottie.loader: loadLottie() + playLottie() from motion.js. Never lottie.loadAnimation() directly, never window.__hfLottie, never a path: URL — each of those renders a blank scene that passes every check.
lottie.inline_as_js: assets/lottie/<name>.js assigning window.L_<name> = {...}. A .json fetched at runtime resolves after the runtime has inspected the page.
lottie._cost_note: lottie-web redraws the whole illustration every frame: two heavy ones took a 20s 1080p render from 1m27 to 3m56 (2.7x). The cap is about render time AND about not turning the cut into a template deck.
lottie._cap_note: Was max_per_video: 3. Raised and re-scoped to PER CHAPTER on 2026-08-04: the creator asked for Lotties 'as much as we can', and the pipeline now builds and draft-renders one chapter at a time, so the render-time cost the old cap protected against is discovered in a 3-minute draft instead of a 40-minute final. The cost is still real (see _cost_note) — the cap is the point at which you must justify the next one, not a target to hit.
lottie.reach_for_it_when: The beat is a NUMBER, COMPARISON, PROCESS, DATE, SHARE or COUNT — anything a photograph cannot state. A ratio (37.8% vs ~1%), a subset inside a set, a date being circled: these are FAILS as flat photos, not missed opportunities. Stock cannot photograph an abstraction; drawing it is the only honest option.
lottie.truth_bar: Drawn art asserts a measurement, so it carries a higher bar than a photograph. Heights, counts and proportions are computed from facts-staging figures and the generator says so in a comment. Anything reading as a published figure must BE one; a decorative proportion that looks like a statistic is a defect. Never fabricate a source document — no invented agency names, seals or legible figures on a frame cited to a real table.

blockframe-9.summary: Centred stack over a full-bleed graded photo. The original system.

swiss-band.summary: Swiss/Vignelli. A fixed 1920x600 photographic band on a 12-column grid, black title bar above, statement hung from a rule below. Flush left, squared corners, no scrim, no text-shadow, TWO type sizes per scene.
swiss-band.notes: The band is a fixed aperture — identical geometry every scene — which unifies nine unrelated photos geometrically instead of with a filter. Dense beats (chip rows, four-row bills, the two-column classifier) must be RESTRUCTURED to fit the 240px statement zone, not shrunk: two type sizes per scene is the rule, from the Vignelli Canon. Vary the aperture across the nine scenes as a sequence, never the same window nine times — that is the anti-sameness engine. Retire the per-scene --tint here: colour is a signifier, not pictorial.

ledger-rail.summary: 300px left rail carrying the scene index (thin weight) + beat label; content left-aligned and ragged right; photo confined to a hard-edged right panel, so no scrim and no text-shadow are needed.

layout.image_relevance: THE SOUND-OFF TEST (hard creator rule, 2026-08-04): with the sound off and the on-screen text stripped, the image alone must tell the viewer what the scene is about. Applied PER LINE, not per chapter — every point in the script got its own line because it is its own idea, so it gets its own picture. Three failures, all shipped at least once before this rule was written: (1) an image that argues with its line (a balanced scale under 'thirty times apart'); (2) one image reused across several points (one photo of books behind the internet claim, the survey AND the 30x gap); (3) an image asserting the wrong place or era (an Indian shopkeeper for Japan's national accounts, a demonetised Rs500 for today's money). When a slot cannot be photographed, change the SOURCE or draw it — never accept a near-miss: @commons for named buildings/institutions/monuments, a Lottie for abstractions.
layout.grade_note: blockframe.css ships .bg { grayscale(.32) brightness(.62) }. Per-scene overrides that go darker to make drawn art readable stack with it and desaturate real photographs into grey mush — the creator rejected exactly this on 2026-08-04 ('it fails to black and white'). If a Lottie needs a darker field, darken BEHIND THE ART, not the whole frame.

_known_benign_note: Empty is the correct state. The one entry ever added — invalid_parent_traversal_in_asset_path — was WRONG, and cost four cuts their browser checks: it reasoned the ../ urls were a static-analysis false positive because the render looked right, which was true. What it missed is that a lint ERROR makes `hyperframes check` SKIP the layout and contrast passes entirely, so those four cuts shipped with WCAG and layout never actually run. Fixed at the root 2026-08-01 by moving blockframe.css to assets/blockframe.css so the urls need no ../ at all. Lesson: 'the output looks fine' does not establish that a finding is benign — check what the finding SUPPRESSES.

qa._vad_note: Silero VAD reports speech onset LATE and quantised: every onset lands on a multiple of 0.032s (its 512-sample window), and the detector adds a systematic positive bias measured at +0.101s median across 92 lines (japanese-money-methods-hi, 2026-08-01). Subtract this bias before comparing against the 0.1s drift target — raw VAD max on that cut was +0.167s (a false FAIL) against a true residual of 0.068s. Re-measure the bias if the VAD model or window changes.
qa._dissolve_note: Sample transitions at BOTH offsets into the overlap. The incoming .stack rises at start+0.30 of a 0.45s dissolve, so a midpoint frame (start+0.225) lands before the incoming text exists and CANNOT see a double-paint — the exact blind spot that let the missing `.scene` stacking context ship. start+0.38 is inside the only ~0.15s window where both scenes' text can be up.
qa._whisper_note: Do NOT derive per-line drift from Whisper segment starts: `base` merged 92 lines into 173 segments and produced a phantom 7.675s outlier. Use Whisper for COVERAGE (gaps, dropped clips), VAD for onsets.

chapter_design._note: The archetype layer for chapter-based (MEDIUM/LONG) cuts. Rationale and the full rule list: vault/knowledge/design-chapter-archetypes.md. Code: tools/scaffold/assets/chapter-design.css. Adopted 2026-08-05 after five draft passes on japanese-money-methods ch1+ch2, creator-approved.

A.use: centred stack, motif full-bleed behind — chapter opens, hand-offs

B.use: the figure owns the frame; rule at the left margin, measure bar under the type

C.use: hard vertical split — type left, artefact full-height right, cropped by the frame edge

D.use: type under a full-width rule, mechanism owning the bottom two-thirds

scene_modifiers.has-photo: REQUIRED on every scene carrying a graded still. Ground -> 38% tint, plate -> aperture, hatch off.
scene_modifiers.art-off: the scene's drawn layer duplicates the photograph; hide it. See rule 8.
scene_modifiers.art-forward: buy the drawn layer back to 52% — only for scenes whose point is a PROPORTION.
scene_modifiers.centred: the archetype's other side is empty, so the split is a hole; re-centre and drop plate/crule/vrule/brule.
scene_modifiers.art-lift: keep the plate's panel lift on a scene whose drawn layer sits on a BRIGHT still (ruled paper, banknotes, a white wardrobe). `.has-photo` turns the plate into an aperture, which is right over a dark photograph and makes ink art light-on-light over a pale one. This is the plate-scoped form of rule 9 — it darkens BEHIND the art and cannot touch the photograph outside the plate rect.

ken_safe_zone._note: The genuinely-always-visible svg window once ken scales the field 1.0->1.16. Art outside it is cropped silently and every check still passes. A .plate makes this moot by declaring its own window — prefer the plate.

art_opacity._important_note: `.has-photo .art` and `.has-photo.art-forward .art` both carry !important, so a per-scene inline opacity on the <svg> is a NO-OP. The only levers that reach the screen are the weight and alpha of the elements INSIDE it.

chapter_design._rail_note: A top rail carrying a chapter title and an 'N / total' scene counter was built and REMOVED at creator request 2026-08-05: the viewer must not be shown that the video is chapter-based or slide-numbered. Do not reintroduce it.
gotchas: stroke-width="N" as an SVG ATTRIBUTE is a no-op — .art .st sets it in CSS and a CSS rule always beats a presentation attribute. Use inline style="stroke-width:N".
A scrolling group needs a clipPath or it rides out of its band into the type.
breathe(dur) quantises to whole out-and-back pairs and rounds UP as often as down — 4.5 yields 6.0s. Ask for a multiple of 3.
A plate must be a LIFTED PANEL, not a transparent rect, or dark art has nothing to read against.

Over a graded still, thin outline scaffolding is not on screen. .30/.52 of a 2-3px stroke at 0.4 alpha survives no encode — draw with SOLID FILLS and strokes of 9px and up, and let the ghost/track shapes be filled rects at ~.2 rather than outlines.

tools/chapter_sheet.py samples a non-Lottie scene at +2.6s. A drawn layer that finishes at +4.4 sheets as a half-built frame and reads as a defect that is not one — assemble the mechanism by about +3.3, or judge that scene from the mp4.
chapter_design.generator: tools/chapter_project.py — builds a chapter project from the shipped cut + a hand-authored chapter.json. Every data-start / data-duration / data-framings / data-track-index, every on-screen string, every .bg and every <audio> row is lifted VERBATIM and only rebased; the spec owns the DESIGN only. It re-reads what it wrote and asserts the rebase before exiting, so a chapter whose durations sum correctly while its internal cuts drift cannot be produced.
chapter_design.one_root_html: A chapter project has exactly ONE root .html and it is index.html. `hyperframes check` only looks for index.html, tools/chapter_sheet.py hardcodes it, and the linter's `multiple_root_compositions` is an ERROR on two root files carrying data-composition-id — so the ch1/ch2 index.html + index-claudedesign.html pair cannot pass a check. In a chapter project index.html is NOT the shipped cut.
chapter_design.measure_position: `.measure-lab.under` / `.measure.under` — left calc(50% - 460px), top 868/910, width 920, height 7. Declared in the stylesheet, not per scene: at the old y742 the bar landed on the icon that variant-A scenes carry inside their stack, and struck its own label through on three consecutive frames of ch4.
